title.zh: 卷366 列傳一百五十三 孙玉庭 蒋攸铦 李鸿宾
title.en: Volume 366 Biographies 153: Sun Yuting, Jiang Youxian, Li Hongbin
title.raw: 卷366 列傳一百五十三 孙玉庭 蒋攸铦 李鸿宾

sentences.zh: 列傳一百五十三

translations.literal: Biographies 153
translations.idiomatic: Biography 153

sentences.zh: 孫玉庭、蔣攸銛、李鴻賓

translations.literal: Sun Yuting, Jiang Youxian, and Li Hongbin
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuting, Jiang Youxian, and Li Hongbin

sentences.zh: 孫玉庭，字寄圃，山東濟寧人。

translations.literal: Sun Yuting, whose style name was Jipu, was a native of Jining in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuting, styled Jipu, came from Jining in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year 40 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and received an appointment as reviser.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，出為山西河東道，父憂去，服闋，補廣西鹽法道。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he went out as intendant of Hedong in Shanxi; he left office on his father's death, and after mourning was reassigned as salt commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 51 he was posted as Hedong circuit intendant in Shanxi; after leaving for his father's mourning and completing the mourning period, he was appointed Guangxi salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，就遷按察使，歷湖南、安徽、湖北布政使，舉發道員胡齊崙侵冒軍需，詔嘉之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiaqing reign he was promoted in place to provincial judicial commissioner, served successively as provincial treasurer of Hunan, Anhui, and Hubei, and exposed the circuit intendant Hu Qilun for embezzling military supplies; the throne praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing he rose to provincial judicial commissioner, then served as treasurer in Hunan, Anhui, and Hubei in turn; he reported the circuit intendant Hu Qilun for embezzling military funds, and the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢廣西巡撫，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi and transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was made governor of Guangxi and then transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 安南國王阮光纘為農耐、阮福映所逼，叩關乞內避，命玉庭馳赴廣西察辦。

translations.literal: The king of Annam, Ruan Guangzan, being pressed by Nong Nai and Nguyen Phuc Anh, knocked at the border to beg refuge within China; Yuting was ordered to hurry to Guangxi to investigate and handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Annamese ruler Ruan Guangzan, harried by Nong Nai and Nguyen Phuc Anh, came to the frontier seeking sanctuary inside the empire; Yuting was commanded to rush to Guangxi to look into the affair.

sentences.zh: 福映已滅光纘，遣使納款，玉庭疏陳其恭順，請受之。

translations.literal: Phuc Anh had already destroyed Guangzan and sent envoys to offer submission; Yuting memorialized that they were respectful and compliant and asked that they be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Phuc Anh had already overthrown Guangzan and sent envoys to submit; Yuting reported their deference and asked that submission be accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋福映請改國名曰南越，仁宗疑之。

translations.literal: Soon Phuc Anh requested to change the state name to Nanyue; the Renzong Emperor was doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Phuc Anh asked to rename the country Nanyue, which aroused the emperor's suspicion.

sentences.zh: 玉庭言：「不可以語言文字阻外夷鄉化之心。

translations.literal: Yuting said: "One must not use language and writing to obstruct the desire of outer barbarians to turn toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Yuting argued: "Language and script should not be used to block foreign peoples from inclining toward civilization.

sentences.zh: 其先有古越裳地，繼並安南。

translations.literal: Their territory formerly included the land of ancient Yuechang, and later they annexed Annam.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands once held the ancient Yuechang region and later absorbed Annam as well.

sentences.zh: 若改號越南，亦與中國南粵舊名有別。

translations.literal: If the name is changed to Yuenan, it is also distinct from the old Chinese name for the southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: If the title is changed to Vietnam, it still differs from the old Chinese designation for the southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 」乃報可。

translations.literal: " The request was then approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court thereupon approved it.

sentences.zh: 廣東海盜日橫，玉庭議防急於剿，請增兵嚴守口岸，禁淡水米糧出海以製之。

translations.literal: Pirates in Guangdong grew daily more rampant; Yuting argued that defense was more urgent than suppression, asked to increase troops and strictly guard the ports, and forbade fresh water and grain to go to sea to restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong pirates were spreading by the day; Yuting held that guarding the coast mattered more than chasing raids, urged more troops at the ports, and barred fresh water and rice from going out to sea to choke them.

sentences.zh: 尋調廣西，十年，復調廣東。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Guangxi; in the tenth year he was transferred back to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Guangxi, and in year 10 returned to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時總督那彥成專意招撫，玉庭意不合，疏陳其弊，謂：「盜非悔罪，特為貪利而來。

translations.literal: At that time the governor-general Nayancheng devoted himself solely to pacification by inducement; Yuting disagreed and memorialized on its abuses, saying: "The bandits are not repenting of crime but come solely for profit.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general Nayancheng was intent on winning pirates over by inducement; Yuting dissented and laid out the harm in a memorial: "These men are not repenting—they come only for gain.

sentences.zh: 官吏貪功，不惜重金為市。

translations.literal: Officials, greedy for merit, do not spare heavy gold to buy them.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for credit, officials do not hesitate to pay them large sums.

sentences.zh: 陽避盜名，陰攖盜實。

translations.literal: Outwardly they shun the name of banditry; inwardly they abet the bandits' substance.
translations.idiomatic: In name they avoid collusion with pirates; in fact they feed the pirates' strength.

sentences.zh: 廢法斂怨，莫此為尤。

translations.literal: To abandon the law and heap up resentment—nothing is worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing breeds resentment and lawlessness more than this.

sentences.zh: 」上韙其言，那彥成由是獲罪。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words, and Nayancheng was punished on that account.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne endorsed his view, and Nayancheng was punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 十三年，英吉利兵船入澳門，總督吳熊光但停貿易，未遣兵驅逐，上斥畏葸，罷熊光，調玉庭貴州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year English warships entered Macao; Governor Wu Xiongguang only halted trade and did not send troops to drive them off; the emperor rebuked his timidity, dismissed Xiongguang, and transferred Yuting to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 British warships entered Macao; Governor Wu Xiongguang merely suspended trade and sent no force to expel them; the emperor denounced his timidity, removed Xiongguang, and moved Yuting to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋百齡至粵，追論熊光，且劾玉庭不以實入告，坐罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon Bailin arrived in Guangdong, pursued the case against Xiongguang, and also impeached Yuting for not reporting the facts; he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Bailin soon came to Guangdong, reopened the case against Xiongguang, and also impeached Yuting for failing to report truthfully; Yuting was cashiered and sent home.

sentences.zh: 已而予官編修，在文穎館行走。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the post of Hanlin compiler and served in the Wenyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was restored as a Hanlin compiler and served in the Wenyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授雲南巡撫，兼署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor of Yunnan and concurrently acting governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was made governor of Yunnan and acting governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 調浙江。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英吉利貢使不原行跪拜禮，廷議以其倔強，遣之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the English tribute mission refused to perform the prostration ceremony; the court debated and, because of their obstinacy, sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 the British tribute embassy declined the kowtow; court debate deemed them defiant and they were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會玉庭入覲，面奏馭夷之道：「妄有乾求，當折以天朝之法度；

translations.literal: When Yuting came to audience he personally memorialized on the way to manage barbarians: "If they presumptuously make demands, they should be checked by the celestial dynasty's standards;
translations.idiomatic: Yuting happened to be at court and spoke on handling foreigners: "Unwarranted demands should be rebuffed by imperial law;

sentences.zh: 歸心恪順，不責以中國之儀文。

translations.literal: if their hearts return in respectful compliance, do not demand of them China's ritual forms.
translations.idiomatic: if they are sincerely compliant, do not insist on Chinese ceremonial forms.

sentences.zh: 」反覆開陳，上意乃解。

translations.literal: " He expounded this repeatedly, and the emperor's mind was set at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " He argued the point at length until the emperor was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，調兩江。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was transferred to the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 漕、鹽、河為江南要政，日臻疲累。

translations.literal: Grain transport, salt, and rivers were the key policies of Jiangnan, and each day grew more exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The grain transport, salt monopoly, and river works were Jiangnan's chief concerns, and all were wearing down.

sentences.zh: 玉庭久任封圻，治尚安靜，整頓江西、湖北引岸緝私，籌款生息，津貼屯丁，減省漕委，隨事為補苴之計，稍稍相安。

translations.literal: Yuting had long held frontier posts and favored quiet governance; he tightened anti-smuggling on the Jiangxi and Hubei distribution banks, raised funds for interest, subsidized transport garrison soldiers, reduced grain-transport deputies, and patched matters as he could, so that things gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: Long experienced on the frontiers, Yuting governed for stability: he tightened salt smuggling controls on the Jiangxi and Hubei banks, raised revolving funds, subsidized transport troops, trimmed grain-transport staff, and patched what he could until affairs eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，特加太子少保銜。

translations.literal: When the Daoguang Emperor acceded, Yuting was specially given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At Daoguang's accession he was specially granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時用尚書英和言，清查直省陋規，立以限制，下疆臣議久遠之法。

translations.literal: At the time, following Minister Ying He's proposal, irregular fees in all provinces were to be investigated and limits set; frontier officials were ordered to devise a lasting method.
translations.idiomatic: The court, following Minister Ying He, ordered a survey of provincial "irregular fees" with fixed limits and told frontier governors to devise durable rules.

sentences.zh: 玉庭疏言：「自古有治人無治法。

translations.literal: Yuting memorialized: "From antiquity there have been men who govern well, not laws that govern well.
translations.idiomatic: Yuting wrote: "Since antiquity good government has depended on good men, not on good laws alone.

sentences.zh: 果督撫兩司皆得人，則大法小廉，自不虞所屬苛取病民；

translations.literal: If governors, treasurers, and judicial commissioners are all the right men, then great law and small integrity follow of themselves, and one need not fear subordinates' harsh exactions harming the people;
translations.idiomatic: If governors and the two commissioners are truly capable, high principle and petty honesty follow naturally and subordinates will not prey on the people;

sentences.zh: 非然者，雖立限制，仍同虛設，弊且滋甚。

translations.literal: otherwise, even if limits are set, they are still empty forms, and abuses will grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise limits are empty forms and abuses only worsen.

sentences.zh: 各省陋規，本幹例禁。

translations.literal: Irregular fees in each province have always been contrary to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial irregular fees have always violated statute.

sentences.zh: 語云：'作法於涼，其弊猶貪。

translations.literal: The saying goes: "If one makes law in a cool season, the abuse is still greed.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, "Make law in cool weather and the abuse is still greed.

sentences.zh: '禁人之取猶不能不取；

translations.literal: " Forbid others to take and they still cannot help but take;
translations.idiomatic: " Forbid taking and men still take;

sentences.zh: 若許之取，勢必益無顧忌。

translations.literal: if you permit taking, they will surely become all the more reckless.
translations.idiomatic: permit it and they become utterly brazen.

sentences.zh: 迨發覺治罪，民已大受其累。

translations.literal: By the time discovery and punishment come, the people have already suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: By the time graft is exposed and punished, the people have long since paid dearly.

sentences.zh: 府、廳、州、縣祿入無多，向來不能不藉陋規為辦公之需，然未聞准其加取於民垂為令甲者，誠以自古無此制祿之經也。

translations.literal: Prefectures, departments, and counties have little formal salary; they have always had to rely on irregular fees for office expenses, yet one never heard of approving added exactions from the people and making them permanent regulations—for truly there has never been such a system of salary by statute.
translations.idiomatic: District magistrates receive little formal pay and have always relied on irregular fees for office costs, yet no one ever made extra levies on the people a standing rule—for there is no ancient precedent for salary fixed that way.

sentences.zh: 伏乞停止查辦，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that the investigation be stopped; the realm would be fortunate indeed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the investigation be halted; the empire would be fortunate.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，詔褒其不媿大臣之言。

translations.literal: " When the memorial arrived, an edict praised his words as befitting a senior minister.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial arrived and an edict praised him for speaking as a great minister should.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，授協辦大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was appointed Grand Secretary without portfolio, while retaining his governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang year 1 he became Grand Secretary without portfolio while keeping the governorship.

sentences.zh: 是年入覲，與玉瀾堂十五老臣宴。

translations.literal: That year he came to audience and was feasted with the fifteen elder statesmen in the Hall of Jade Ripples.
translations.idiomatic: That year he attended court and dined with the fifteen elder ministers in the Hall of Jade Ripples.

sentences.zh: 帝詢淮鹽疏銷之策，玉庭言：「漢口為淮南售鹽總岸，向來船到隨時交易，是以暢銷。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about measures to revive sluggish Huai salt sales; Yuting said: "Hankou is the chief bank for Huainan salt; formerly when ships arrived trade was conducted at once, and therefore sales flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Asked how to revive Huai salt sales, Yuting said: "Hankou is Huainan's main market; ships once traded on arrival, and salt sold freely.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆中立封輪法，挨次輪售，私鹽乘間侵越。

translations.literal: Since the mid-Qianlong period a rotating monopoly was established and sales went in turn; private salt seized the gaps and encroached.
translations.idiomatic: Since mid-Qianlong a sealed rotation system sold in strict order; smugglers filled the gaps.

sentences.zh: 」因臚陳六害，請復舊章，從之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon set forth six harms and asked to restore the old regulations; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " He listed six harms and asked to restore the old rules; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 又言漕糧浮收不能禁革，不如明與八折為便。

translations.literal: He also said that the excess collection on tribute grain could not be abolished, and that it would be better to fix an explicit twenty-percent rate.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that illegal surcharges on tribute grain could not be stamped out and proposed an explicit twenty-percent levy instead.

sentences.zh: 御史王家相奏言事類加賦，侍郎姚文田、湯金釗亦論之，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Jiaxiang memorialized that this resembled adding tax; Vice Ministers Yao Wentian and Tang Jinzhang also objected, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Jiaxiang called it a hidden tax increase; Vice Ministers Yao Wentian and Tang Jinzhang joined the debate, and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 然州縣困於丁費，浮收仍難禁絕，胥吏上下其手，專累良懦，因玉庭議不行，疆臣不敢復請；

translations.literal: Yet districts were strained by labor fees and excess collection remained hard to stop; clerks manipulated accounts above and below, burdening only the honest and weak; because Yuting's plan failed, frontier officials dared not propose again;
translations.idiomatic: Districts still strained under labor charges; surcharges persisted; clerks rigged the books and honest taxpayers bore the cost; with Yuting's plan shelved, governors dared not raise it again;

sentences.zh: 至同治初，始定漕耗，卒如玉庭議。

translations.literal: only in the early Tongzhi period was the transport surcharge finally fixed, ultimately as Yuting had urged.
translations.idiomatic: not until early Tongzhi was the transport surcharge fixed—essentially as Yuting had proposed.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜體仁閣大學士，留任如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Eminence, retaining his post as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he entered the Grand Secretariat at the Hall of Literary Eminence while keeping his post.

sentences.zh: 會高家堰決，河督張文浩遣戍，部議玉庭革職，詔念前勞，寬之，留任。

translations.literal: When the Gaojiayan embankment burst, River Director Zhang Wenhao was banished; the ministry proposed dismissing Yuting; an edict recalled his past service, showed leniency, and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaojiayan broke, River Director Zhang Wenhao was exiled; the ministry wanted Yuting removed; the throne cited his past service, showed mercy, and kept him.

sentences.zh: 尋復以借黃濟運無效，褫職，予編修休致。

translations.literal: Soon he was again stripped of office for the failure of borrowing the Yellow River to aid transport; he was given compiler rank and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he lost rank again because diverting the Yellow River to feed the canal failed; he was reduced to compiler and retired.

sentences.zh: 戶部复劾其不行海運，而河病運阻，責償滯漕剝運費十之七，命留濬運河。

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue again impeached him for not implementing sea transport while river sickness blocked the canal; he was ordered to repay seven-tenths of delayed tribute and stripped transport fees, and was ordered to remain dredging the canal.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue impeached him again for refusing sea transport while the canal sickened; he must repay seven-tenths of delayed grain costs and stay to dredge the canal.

sentences.zh: 工竣，回籍。

translations.literal: When the work was finished he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When dredging finished he went home.

sentences.zh: 十四年，重宴鹿鳴，加四品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was again feasted at the Deer-Ming banquet and given a fourth-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was honored again at the Deer-Ming banquet and given a fourth-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十有三。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, at the age of eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died, aged eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 子善寶，以舉人廕生授刑部員外郎，官至江蘇巡撫；

translations.literal: His son Shanbao, by hereditary privilege as a juren, was appointed a vice director in the Ministry of Punishments and rose to governor of Jiangsu;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shanbao, a juren by privilege appointment, became a vice director of Punishments and rose to Jiangsu governor;

sentences.zh: 瑞珍，道光三年進士，由翰林官至戶部尚書，諡文定。

translations.literal: Ruizhen, a jinshi of the third year of Daoguang, rose from Hanlin to Minister of Revenue, posthumous name Wending.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizhen, jinshi in Daoguang year 3, rose from Hanlin to Minister of Revenue with the posthumous title Wending.

sentences.zh: 孫毓溎，道光二十四年一甲一名進士，官至浙江按察使；

translations.literal: His grandson Yuzhi, top jinshi of the first rank in the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang, rose to provincial judicial commissioner of Zhejiang;
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Yuzhi, top jinshi in Daoguang year 24, became Zhejiang judicial commissioner;

sentences.zh: 毓汶亦以一甲二名進士，官至兵部尚書，自有傳。

translations.literal: Yuwen also took second place in the top trio and rose to Minister of War; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen took second in the top trio and became Minister of War; he has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 曾孫楫，咸豐二年進士，翰林院庶吉士，官至順天府尹。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Ji, jinshi in the second year of Xianfeng, Hanlin bachelor, rose to prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson Ji, Xianfeng year 2 jinshi and Hanlin bachelor, became Shuntian prefect.

sentences.zh: 四世並歷清要，家門之盛，北方士族無與埒焉。

translations.literal: Four generations all held eminent posts; the family's eminence had no peer among northern gentry clans.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations held high office; no northern clan matched their standing.

sentences.zh: 蔣攸銛，字礪堂，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Jiang Youxian, styled Litang, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youxian, styled Litang, belonged to the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 先世由浙江遷遼東，從入關，居寶坻。

translations.literal: His ancestors moved from Zhejiang to Liaodong, followed the conquest, and settled in Baodi.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears moved from Zhejiang to Liaodong, entered the pass with the dynasty, and settled in Baodi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十九年，成進士，年甫十九，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi at only nineteen, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year 49 he passed the jinshi at nineteen, entered Hanlin as a bachelor, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，遷御史，敢言有聲，受仁宗知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing he was promoted to censor; his bold speech won renown and he gained the Renzong Emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing he became a censor, gained fame for outspokenness, and won the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為江西吉南贛道，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out as intendant of Jinan-Gan in Jiangxi and acted as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was posted as Jinan-Gan intendant in Jiangxi and acted as judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，廣昌齋匪廖幹用作亂，攸銛率兵平之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Zhai bandit Liao Ganxing rebelled at Guangchang; Youxian led troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the Zhai sect rebel Liao Ganxing rose at Guangchang; Youxian led troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 疆臣上其功，會丁母憂去。

translations.literal: Frontier officials reported his merit, but he left on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The governor reported his merit, but he left for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 十年，特起署廣東惠潮嘉道，歷江西按察使、雲南布政使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was specially summoned to act as intendant of Huichao-Cha in Guangdong, then served as Jiangxi judicial commissioner and Yunnan treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was specially recalled to act as Huichao-Cha intendant in Guangdong, then served as Jiangxi judicial commissioner and Yunnan treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十四年，調江蘇，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Jiangsu and promptly promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he moved to Jiangsu and was promoted governor on the spot.

sentences.zh: 調浙江，擢江南河道總督，以不諳河務辭，詔回原任。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhejiang, he was promoted to Director-General of Jiangnan Rivers but declined on grounds of unfamiliarity with river work; an edict sent him back to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Zhejiang, he was made Jiangnan River Director but declined as unskilled in hydraulics; the court returned him to his old post.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he became governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 嚴於治盜，遴勤幹文武大員駐廣、肇、韶、連諸郡居中之地，分路搜截，飭州縣官赴鄉勸導耆老，使境內不得藏奸，舉劾嚴明，吏皆用命。

translations.literal: Strict in suppressing bandits, he chose diligent civil and military officers to station at central points in Guangzhou, Zhaoqing, Shaoguan, and Lianzhou, searched by separate routes, ordered district magistrates into the countryside to persuade elders, forbade harboring criminals within their jurisdictions, and made promotions and dismissals strict so that officials obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He cracked down hard on pirates, posted able civil and military officers at hubs in Guang, Zhao, Shao, and Lian, swept by divided routes, sent magistrates to coax village elders, barred sheltering criminals, and enforced strict promotion and dismissal so officials obeyed.

sentences.zh: 歷擒匪盜七百馀名，自首者許自新，特詔褒獎。

translations.literal: In succession he captured more than seven hundred bandits; those who surrendered were allowed to reform; a special edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He captured over seven hundred bandits; surrenders were spared; the throne specially commended him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，應詔陳言，略曰：「我朝累代功德在民，而亂民愍不畏法，變出意外，此皆由於吏治不修所致。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, responding to an imperial call for memorials, he wrote in summary: "Our dynasty's accumulated merit rests with the people, yet disorderly folk pity nothing and fear no law; unexpected changes arise—all because official discipline is not maintained.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, answering an imperial request, he wrote: "The dynasty's merit rests with the people, yet lawless men fear nothing and crises erupt—all from slack governance.

sentences.zh: 臣觀近日道、府、州、縣，貪酷者少而委靡者多。

translations.literal: I observe that recently among circuit, prefectural, and county officials, the cruel and grasping are few while the slack and spiritless are many.
translations.idiomatic: Of late, circuit and county officials are rarely cruel but often listless.

sentences.zh: 夫闒冗之釀患，與貪酷等。

translations.literal: Slack incompetence breeds harm equal to cruelty and grasping.
translations.idiomatic: Listlessness harms the realm as much as cruelty.

sentences.zh: 竊以為方今急務，莫先於察吏，而欲振積習，必用破格之勸懲。

translations.literal: I believe the urgent task today is first to inspect officials; to shake entrenched habits one must use extraordinary rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Today's urgent need is inspecting officials; to break habit requires exceptional reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 凡貪酷者固應嚴參，平庸者亦隨時勒休改用，勿俟大計始行覈辦。

translations.literal: The cruel should of course be impeached severely; the mediocre should also be compelled to retire and reassigned at any time—do not wait for the triennial review to act.
translations.idiomatic: The cruel must be impeached; the mediocre should be forced to retire when seen—do not wait for the grand evaluation.

sentences.zh: 其有勤能者，即請旨優獎。

translations.literal: Those who are diligent and capable should at once be specially rewarded by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: The diligent should receive prompt imperial reward.

sentences.zh: 果道、府、州、縣得人，則禍亂之萌自息。

translations.literal: If circuit, prefectural, and county posts are well filled, the seeds of calamity will die of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: With good men in circuit and county posts, trouble dies in the bud.

sentences.zh: 」次年，又上疏曰：「道府由牧令起家者十之二三，由部員外擢者十之七八。

translations.literal: " The next year he memorialized again: "Of prefects and circuit intendants, two or three tenths rise from district magistracies and seven or eight tenths from ministry vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: " Next year he added: "Only two or three in ten prefects and intendants come from magistracies; seven or eight come from ministry posts.

sentences.zh: 聞近來司員少卓著之才，由於滿洲之廕生太易，漢員之捐班太多。

translations.literal: I hear that lately ministry clerks show little outstanding talent, because Manchu hereditary appointments are too easy and Han purchased offices are too many.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry clerks lately lack talent—Manchu inheritance is too easy, Han purchased posts too many.

sentences.zh: 請飭部臣隨時考覈，其不宜於部務者，以同知、通判分發各省，使練民事，部曹亦可疏通。

translations.literal: I ask that ministry officials examine them regularly; those unfit for ministry work should be sent as subprefects and circuit deputies to the provinces to learn civilian affairs, and the ministry ranks may also be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministries review staff; the unfit should go to provinces as subprefects to learn civil affairs and clear the ministries.

sentences.zh: 今之人才沉於下位者多矣，請飭大臣薦達，擇其名實相副者擢用。

translations.literal: Many able men today are sunk in low posts; I ask that great ministers recommend and promote those whose reputation matches their substance.
translations.idiomatic: Talent languishes below; let senior ministers recommend the worthy for promotion.

sentences.zh: 抑臣更有請者，任事之與專擅，有義利之分，若任事而以專擅罪之，人皆推諉以自全矣。

translations.literal: Moreover I have another request: between fulfilling duty and acting arbitrarily there is a distinction of righteousness and profit; if fulfilling duty is punished as arbitrariness, all will shirk responsibility to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Between duty and arbitrariness lies right and profit; punish duty as arrogance and all will shirk to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 協恭之與黨援，有公私之別，如協恭而以黨援目之，人且立異以遠嫌矣。

translations.literal: Between cooperative respect and faction there is public versus private; if cooperation is labeled faction, men will stand apart to avoid suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Cooperation differs from cliques; call cooperation faction and men will stand apart to avoid suspicion.

sentences.zh: 此近今之積習，為大臣者當力除之。

translations.literal: These are recent entrenched habits; great ministers should strive to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: These are recent habits great ministers must uproot.

sentences.zh: 至翰林儒臣，務在崇正學，黜浮華，養成明體達用之才，不必以文章課殿最。

translations.literal: As for Hanlin scholar-officials, the aim should be to honor orthodox learning, reject flashy display, and nurture talent that understands principle and applies it—there is no need to rank them by literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin scholars should honor orthodox learning, reject display, and train men of practical principle—not rank them by essays alone.

sentences.zh: 科道為耳目之官，敷陳能否得體，糾劾是否為公，詢事考言，難逃洞鑑。

translations.literal: Censors and remonstrators are the court's eyes and ears; whether their presentations are apt and their impeachments just can be judged by inquiry and examination—they cannot escape scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Censors are the court's eyes and ears; fitness of memorials and fairness of impeachment are plain upon inquiry.

sentences.zh: 其有卓越清正者，當由京堂而擢卿貳，與翰詹參用。

translations.literal: Those outstanding in integrity should rise from capital director to vice minister and be used together with Hanlin and academicians.
translations.idiomatic: The exceptionally upright should rise from capital director to vice minister alongside Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 用人之道，因才因地因時，臣下無可市之恩，君上有特操之鑑。

translations.literal: The way to employ men is to suit talent, place, and time; subordinates have no favor to sell, and the sovereign has a distinctive judgment of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Employ men by talent, place, and time; servants must not trade favors, and the ruler keeps his own measure.

sentences.zh: 人無求備，政在集思，此之謂也。

translations.literal: One does not demand completeness in men; government lies in gathering counsel—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Do not demand perfection in men; good government pools counsel—that is the point.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial arrived, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial arrived and the emperor commended it.

sentences.zh: 英吉利兵船入內洋，攸銛飭停貿易，乃聽命引去。

translations.literal: English warships entered the inner seas; Youxian ordered trade halted, and they then obeyed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When British warships entered coastal waters, Youxian halted trade until they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 請禁民人為洋人服役，洋行不許建洋式房屋，鋪商不得用洋字店號，清查商欠，不准無身家者濫充洋商，及內地人私往洋館，並如議行。

translations.literal: He asked to forbid commoners to serve foreigners, forbid foreign firms to build Western-style houses, forbid shops to use foreign characters in trade names, investigate merchant debts, forbid men without property to serve as foreign merchants at will, and forbid inland people to visit foreign compounds privately—all were carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He banned Chinese service to foreigners, Western-style foreign firm buildings, foreign shop signs, lax licensing of foreign merchants, private visits to foreign compounds, and enforced debt audits—all as proposed.

sentences.zh: 商人負暹羅國貨價，以官錢代償，既而貢使來繳還。

translations.literal: Merchants owed the price of goods to Siam; official funds repaid it on their behalf, and later the tribute envoy came to pay it back.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants owed Siam for goods; the government paid, and the Siamese tribute mission later repaid.

sentences.zh: 攸銛以奉旨頒給，乃示懷柔，不得復收回，卻之，詔嘉其得體。

translations.literal: Youxian, because an edict had ordered the disbursement, held that this showed appeasement and the money could not be taken back; he declined it, and an edict praised his tact.
translations.idiomatic: Youxian held the funds were a gift of grace under imperial order and could not be reclaimed; he refused repayment, and the court praised his propriety.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，調四川總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he became governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四川兵故驕縱，一裁以法。

translations.literal: Sichuan troops had long been arrogant and unruly; he cut them all to law.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan troops had grown insubordinate; he disciplined them strictly.

sentences.zh: 民多帶刀劍，禁鄉村設爐制兵刃。

translations.literal: The people commonly carried swords; he forbade villages to set up furnaces to forge weapons.
translations.idiomatic: As people went armed, he barred rural forges for weapons.

sentences.zh: 城市編牌取結，有犯連坐。

translations.literal: In cities he organized household registers and bonds; offenders were punished by joint liability.
translations.idiomatic: In cities he required household registers and surety bonds with collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 以義倉租息助灌縣都江堰歲修，禁派捐累民。

translations.literal: He used the interest from charity granaries to assist the annual repair of the Dujiangyan at Guanxian, and forbade levies that burdened the people.
translations.idiomatic: Charity-granary interest funded Dujiangyan upkeep at Guanxian, and he banned oppressive levies.

sentences.zh: 重修文翁石室，興學造士。

translations.literal: He rebuilt the Stone Chamber of Wen Weng and promoted learning to nurture scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Wen Weng Stone Chamber and fostered education.

sentences.zh: 言官請禁非刑，飭屬銷毀違法刑具，而嚴戒縱匪，不得博寬厚虛名，貽閭閻實害。

translations.literal: When remonstrators asked to forbid illegal torture, he ordered subordinates to destroy unlawful instruments of punishment, and strictly warned against indulging bandits to win a false reputation for leniency, thereby harming the people in fact.
translations.idiomatic: On calls to ban torture, he ordered illegal implements destroyed and warned officials not to coddle bandits for a lenient name while harming the people.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，率土司頭目入都祝嘏，賞賚有加。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he led native chieftains to the capital to offer congratulations; rewards were increased.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he led tribal chiefs to court for celebrations and received extra rewards.

sentences.zh: 時因慶典，普免天下積欠錢糧，獨四川無欠可免，詔嘉其撫綏有方，予優敘。

translations.literal: At the time, because of a celebration, accumulated tax arrears throughout the realm were remitted; Sichuan alone had no arrears to remit; an edict praised his effective pacification and granted preferential treatment.
translations.idiomatic: A general tax amnesty for celebrations found no arrears in Sichuan; the court praised his governance and gave him preferment.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，仁宗崩，入謁梓宮，宣宗諭褒為守兼優，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Renzong Emperor died; he came to pay respects at the coffin, and the Daoguang Emperor praised him as excellent in both civil and military administration and added Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong died in year 25, Youxian attended the bier; Daoguang praised his civil and military record and made him Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，召授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang year 2 he was recalled as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 尋授直隸總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 值水災，請截南漕四十萬石，賑款先後二百萬兩，逾年賑事竣。

translations.literal: When flood struck, he asked to divert four hundred thousand piculs of southern tribute grain and disbursed two million taels in relief in succession; within a year relief was completed.
translations.idiomatic: During floods he diverted 400,000 piculs of southern grain and spent two million taels on relief, finishing within a year.

sentences.zh: 時方治畿輔水利，命侍郎張文浩蒞其事，尋以程含章代之，攸銛與合疏言東西兩淀，大清、永定、子牙、南北運五河，及天津海口、千里堤，不可緩之工，請部撥銀一百二十萬兩；

translations.literal: At the time waterworks in the capital region were under repair; Vice Minister Zhang Wenhao was ordered to oversee, soon replaced by Cheng Hanzhang; Youxian jointly memorialized that work on the eastern and western marshes, the Daqing, Yongding, Ziya, and north-south transport rivers, the Tianjin estuary, and the Thousand-Li Embankment could not be delayed, and asked the ministry to allocate 1.2 million taels;
translations.idiomatic: While Zhili waterworks were underway, he and Cheng Hanzhang memorialized urgent work on the eastern and western marshes, five major rivers, Tianjin harbor, and the Thousand-Li Dike, requesting 1.2 million taels;

sentences.zh: 又疏陳千里堤章程，規复兩淀垡船汊夫，移改管河員弁駐所，添建巡防堡房。

translations.literal: He also memorialized regulations for the Thousand-Li Embankment, restoring marsh boats and channel laborers for the two marshes, moving river officials posts, and adding patrol forts.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed Thousand-Li Dike rules, restored marsh labor and patrol posts, and relocated river officers.

sentences.zh: 並如議行。

translations.literal: All were carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 命協辦大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Secretary without portfolio while retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand Secretary without portfolio while keeping Zhili.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜體仁閣大學士，充軍機大臣，管理刑部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Eminence, served on the Grand Council, and managed the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he entered the Grand Secretariat, joined the Grand Council, and headed Punishments.

sentences.zh: 以回疆平，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Because the Muslim frontier was pacified, he was given Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: With the Muslim frontier pacified, he received Senior Guardian rank.

sentences.zh: 七年，授兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he became governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 疏言總督於河務非專責，與河臣同治，徒掣其肘，請毋庸駐清江浦​​，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the governor-general was not solely responsible for river affairs and that joint administration with the river director only hampered him; he asked not to be required to reside at Qingjiangpu, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the governor-general should not share river duties with the river director or be tied to Qingjiangpu; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 時清水不能敵黃，漕運屢阻。

translations.literal: At the time clear water could not overcome the Yellow River silt, and grain transport was repeatedly blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Clear water could not beat Yellow River silt, and the canal transport stalled repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 攸銛初在浙，不主海運，至是見河、漕交困，試行海運便利，遂請續行，並預儲銀六十萬兩，備河運盤壩之用。

translations.literal: Youxian, when in Zhejiang, had not favored sea transport; now seeing rivers and transport both in distress, he tried sea transport and found it convenient, and therefore asked to continue it and set aside six hundred thousand taels in reserve for canal transport and dam work.
translations.idiomatic: Once opposed to sea transport in Zhejiang, he now found it workable amid canal crisis and asked to continue it with 600,000 taels reserved for dam work.

sentences.zh: 廷議方主倒塘濟運法，且疑其畏難便私，不許。

translations.literal: Court debate then favored the method of drawing from the storage ponds to aid transport, and suspected him of shirking difficulty for private convenience; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: The court favored pond-diversion transport and suspected him of shirking for private ease; it refused.

sentences.zh: 攸銛疏辯，極言倒塘之不足恃，上終不以為然，姑許海運，而禁言盤壩。

translations.literal: Youxian memorialized in defense, strongly stating that pond diversion could not be relied on; the emperor was not convinced, provisionally allowed sea transport, but forbade talk of dam work.
translations.idiomatic: Youxian argued pond diversion was unreliable; the emperor only grudgingly allowed sea transport and barred talk of dams.

sentences.zh: 未幾，海運亦罷。

translations.literal: Before long sea transport was also abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Sea transport was soon abandoned as well.

sentences.zh: 以張格爾就擒，追論贊畫功，晉太子太傅。

translations.literal: Because Jahangir was captured, his planning merit was reviewed and he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: With Jahangir captured, his planning was rewarded with Grand Mentor rank.

sentences.zh: 黃玉林者，鹽梟巨魁，以儀徵老虎頸為窟穴，長江千里，呼吸皆通，詔責嚴捕，玉林投首，乞捕私自效。

translations.literal: Huang Yulin was a great salt smuggling chief who used Laohujing at Yizheng as his lair; along a thousand li of the Yangtze all connections breathed together; an edict ordered strict capture; Yulin surrendered and begged to serve by capturing smugglers himself.
translations.idiomatic: Salt boss Huang Yulin ran Laohujing at Yizheng and controlled the Yangtze; ordered seized, he surrendered and offered to hunt smugglers.

sentences.zh: 十年，攸銛病，乞假，假滿，召回京供職，而玉林复圖販私，攸銛疏請嚴治，發遣新疆，尋复慮其潛回滋事，密請處絞。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Youxian fell ill and asked leave; when leave ended he was recalled to serve in the capital, but Yulin again plotted smuggling; Youxian memorialized asking severe punishment and banishment to Xinjiang; soon fearing he might slip back and cause trouble, he secretly asked that he be executed by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, ill on leave then recalled, Youxian found Yulin smuggling again, sent him to Xinjiang, then secretly sought his execution.

sentences.zh: 詔誅玉林，切責攸銛苟且從事，嚴議褫職，加恩降兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: An edict executed Yulin, sharply rebuked Youxian for perfunctory handling, and after severe deliberation stripped his office, but as grace reduced him to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin was executed; Youxian was rebuked for lax handling, stripped of office, then mercifully reduced to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 未至京，卒於途，優詔軫惜，依尚書例賜卹。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capital he died on the road; a gracious edict expressed grief, and funeral gifts were given according to the rank of minister.
translations.idiomatic: He died en route; the throne mourned him and granted ministerial funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 攸銛精敏強識，與人一面一言，閱數十年記憶不爽。

translations.literal: Youxian was keen and had a strong memory; after one meeting and one remark with a person, decades later his memory did not err.
translations.idiomatic: Youxian was sharp-witted; one meeting sufficed for decades of accurate recall.

sentences.zh: 勇於任事，不唯阿。

translations.literal: He was bold in undertaking affairs and did not merely agree.
translations.idiomatic: He acted boldly and would not simply agree.

sentences.zh: 尤長於察吏，薦賢如不及，所舉後多以事功名節著。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at inspecting officials and recommending the worthy as if he could not keep pace; those he recommended later often won merit, fame, and integrity in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at spotting officials and recommending talent urgently; many he advanced later distinguished themselves.

sentences.zh: 子霨遠，官至貴州巡撫，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Xiyuan rose to governor of Guizhou and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiyuan became Guizhou governor and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 李鴻賓，字鹿蘋，江西德化人。

translations.literal: Li Hongbin, styled Luping, was a native of Dehua in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongbin, styled Luping, came from Dehua in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: A Jiaqing year 6 jinshi, he entered Hanlin and became a reviser.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 十八年，巡視東漕。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he inspected eastern grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he inspected eastern grain transport.

sentences.zh: 會林清之變，數疏陳時政利弊；

translations.literal: At the time of the Lin Qing incident he repeatedly memorialized on the advantages and harms of current policy;
translations.idiomatic: During the Lin Qing affair he repeatedly memorialized on policy;

sentences.zh: 又以山東、河南、直隸毗連之地，頻年遭兵，條上善後事，始受仁宗知。

translations.literal: he also, because Shandong, Henan, and Zhili were contiguous and had suffered warfare for years in succession, set forth items for postwar recovery and first gained the Renzong Emperor notice.
translations.idiomatic: he also laid out recovery plans for war-ravaged Shandong, Henan, and Zhili and first won the emperor notice.

sentences.zh: 命偕河督吳璥、巡撫同興按河督李亨特貪劣不職狀，得實以聞。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with River Director Wu Jun and Governor Tongxing to investigate River Director Li Hengte corruption and incompetence; the facts were established and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered with Wu Jun and Tongxing to investigate Li Hengte corruption, he proved the case.

sentences.zh: 十九年，超授東河副總河。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted out of turn to deputy director-general of the Eastern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he was leap-promoted to Eastern Rivers deputy director.

sentences.zh: 時微山湖蓄水盡涸，運河淤塞。

translations.literal: At the time the Weishan Lake stored water was entirely dry and the Grand Canal silted shut.
translations.idiomatic: Weishan Lake had dried and the Grand Canal was choked.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓自巡漕時講求疏泉濟運之策，至是疏瀹上游，湖水通暢，瀦蓄充盈，漕運無阻，被褒獎，命赴睢工，會同吳璥塞河。

translations.literal: Hongbin, since his grain-transport inspection days, had studied measures to open springs and aid transport; now he dredged the upper reaches, the lake water flowed freely, storage was full, and grain transport was unimpeded; he was praised and ordered to the Sui works to join Wu Jun in blocking the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hongbin dredged upstream as he had long urged; the lake refilled, transport flowed, and he was sent to join Wu Jun at the Sui breach.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Director-General of the Eastern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he became Eastern Rivers director-general.

sentences.zh: 由諫官不三年而膺方面，為時所罕。

translations.literal: From remonstrator to frontier governor in less than three years was rare in the age.
translations.idiomatic: From censor to frontier governor in under three years was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，賜金治喪，予諭祭，異數也。

translations.literal: Soon he left on his mother mourning; gold was granted for the funeral and an edict ordered sacrifices—an exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother with imperial gold and ordered sacrifices—rare honor.

sentences.zh: 服闋，署禮部、兵部侍郎，命赴河南、山東讞獄，並察黃河、運河、湖水情形。

translations.literal: After mourning he acted as vice minister of Rites and War, was ordered to Henan and Shandong to judge cases, and to inspect the Yellow River, canal, and lake conditions.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as acting vice minister and inspected rivers and judged cases in Henan and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，署廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he acted as governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he acted as Guangdong governor.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授漕運總督，復調河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Director-General of Grain Transport and again transferred to Director-General of the Eastern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he became grain transport director, then Eastern Rivers director again.

sentences.zh: 河決蘭陽、儀封，命偕尚書吳璥治之，鴻賓專駐儀封。

translations.literal: When the river burst at Lanyang and Yifeng, he was ordered together with Minister Wu Jun to repair it; Hongbin was stationed specially at Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the river broke at Lanyang and Yifeng, he worked with Wu Jun while based at Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 會北岸馬營壩復決，合疏言馬營土質沙松，河溜尚勁，未能遽定壩基，被詰責，遂自陳不胜河督之任。

translations.literal: When the north-bank Maying dam burst again, they jointly memorialized that Maying soil was sandy and loose and the current still strong, so the dam base could not quickly be fixed; he was rebuked and then himself stated he was unfit for the post of river director.
translations.idiomatic: After Maying burst again, their plea that sandy soil and swift current delayed the work brought rebuke; Hongbin confessed himself unfit for river director.

sentences.zh: 詔斥其見吳璥辦工遲緩，慮同獲咎，預為地步，褫職，予郎中銜，留河南專司大工錢糧。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him for seeing Wu Jun work slow and fearing shared blame, making preparations in advance; he was stripped of office, given the rank of director, and left in Henan solely to manage great-work funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The court said he feared sharing Wu Jun blame and hedged; he was cashiered to director rank to manage Henan works funds.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，命營山東運河事務，兼署山東巡撫，專駐張秋，籌備趲運事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was ordered to manage Shandong canal affairs, concurrently acting as governor of Shandong, stationed specially at Zhangqiu to prepare rush transport.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he ran Shandong canal affairs as acting governor from Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 尋授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Anhui governor.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，調漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to Director-General of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang year 1 he returned to grain transport director.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he became Huguang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 初，湖廣行銷淮鹽，用封輪法，大商壟斷，小商向隅，甫改開輪，又有跌價爭售之害。

translations.literal: Initially Huguang marketed Huai salt under the sealed rotation method; great merchants monopolized and small merchants were excluded; when rotation was opened, there was also the harm of price-cutting competition in sales.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Huai salt had been a sealed monopoly hurting small dealers; opening rotation brought price wars.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓請設公司，簽商經理，無論鹽船到岸先後，小商隨到隨售，大商按所到各家計引均銷。

translations.literal: Hongbin asked to establish a company with contracted merchants to manage it; regardless of whether salt ships reached the bank first or later, small merchants could sell as they arrived, and great merchants would distribute sales evenly by quota according to each firm arrivals.
translations.idiomatic: Hongbin proposed a chartered company so small sellers could trade on arrival while big merchants split quotas evenly.

sentences.zh: 試行兩月後，販運踴躍，著為令。

translations.literal: After a two-month trial, transport and sales were vigorous, and it was made a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: A two-month trial revived trade, and the rule was fixed.

sentences.zh: 時議折漕以資治河，鴻賓疏言徵收折色，弊竇叢生，莫若令民間完交本色，由州縣賣米易銀，轉解河工，詔以易啟抑勒捏價、加收平色諸弊，未允行。

translations.literal: At the time there was debate on converting tribute grain to fund river work; Hongbin memorialized that collecting commuted payments bred countless abuses, and that it would be better to let the people deliver grain in kind and have districts sell rice for silver to forward to river works; an edict held this would easily give rise to extortion, forced prices, and extra surcharges, and it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: Debated grain commutation for river funds, Hongbin preferred in-kind grain sold locally for silver; the court feared extortion and refused.

sentences.zh: 調兩廣總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 廣東通商久，號為利藪。

translations.literal: Guangdong had long traded with foreigners and was called a profit pool.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong trade had long made it a profit haven.

sentences.zh: 自嘉慶以來，英吉利國勢日強，漸跋扈。

translations.literal: Since Jiaqing, England power grew daily stronger and gradually became overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jiaqing Britain grew stronger and more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 故事，十三行洋商有缺，十二家聯保承充，虧帑則攤償。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a vacancy occurred among the thirteen licensed foreign merchants, twelve firms jointly guaranteed the replacement, and deficits were shared in repayment.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen Canton licensed merchants filled vacancies by joint guarantee, sharing any deficits.

sentences.zh: 英領事顛地知洋行獲利厚，欲以洋廝容阿華充商，諸商不允，乃賄鴻賓得之。

translations.literal: The English consul Dent knew foreign firms profited heavily and wished to install the foreign clerk Rong Ahua as merchant; the merchants refused, so he bribed Hongbin and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Consul Dent wanted his clerk Rong Ahua licensed; merchants refused, so he bribed Hongbin.

sentences.zh: 顛地曰：「吾以為總督若何嚴重，詎消數万金便營私耶！

translations.literal: Dent said: "I thought a governor-general would be so stern—who knew a few tens of thousands in gold would buy private favor!
translations.idiomatic: Dent said, "I thought governors were formidable—who knew tens of thousands of taels could buy them off!"

sentences.zh: 」於是始輕中國官吏。

translations.literal: " From this he first looked down on Chinese officials.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on foreigners despised Chinese officials.

sentences.zh: 容阿華尋以淫侈耗貲逃，勿獲，官帑無著，不能責諸商代償，乃以抽分法為彌補，眾商藉以漁利，夷情不服，日益多事。

translations.literal: Rong Ahua soon fled after dissolute spending; he could not be caught, official funds had no recourse, the other merchants could not be compelled to repay, so a profit-sharing method was used to cover the loss; the merchants used it to fish for profit, foreign sentiment was dissatisfied, and affairs daily grew more troublesome.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Ahua fled after extravagance; public funds were lost; merchants could not cover it, so profit-sharing patches bred disputes and worsening relations.

sentences.zh: 鴉片流行日廣，漏銀外洋，鴻賓屢疏陳查禁之法及禁種罌粟，並增築虎門大角砲台，以資控禦，而奉行具文，未有實效。

translations.literal: Opium spread daily wider and silver leaked abroad; Hongbin repeatedly memorialized methods to investigate and forbid it and to forbid cultivating poppies, and also added fortifications at Humen and Dajiao, to aid control, but enforcement was nominal and there was no real effect.
translations.idiomatic: Opium and silver drain led Hongbin to propose bans and Humen forts, but enforcement was hollow.

sentences.zh: 十年，協辦大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary without portfolio while retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he became Grand Secretary without portfolio while keeping Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，崖州黎匪亂，鴻賓駐雷州，令提督劉榮慶、總兵孫得發剿平之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Li bandits rebelled at Yazhou in Qiong; Hongbin stationed at Leizhou and ordered Grand Coordinator Liu Rongqing and Regional Commander Sun Defa to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Qiongzhou Li rebels rose; Hongbin at Leizhou sent Liu Rongqing and Sun Defa to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉光三奏廣東匪徒立會滋擾，鴻賓疏陳：「無三點會名目，惟搶劫打單，勒索民財，根株未絕。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Guangsan memorialized that Guangdong bandits formed societies and stirred trouble; Hongbin memorialized: "There is no society called the Three-Point Society, only robbery and posting demands to extort the people wealth; the roots are not yet cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangsan reported secret societies; Hongbin replied there was no Three-Point Society, only robbery and extortion still rooted.

sentences.zh: 隨時訪拿，準自首免罪。

translations.literal: Capture at any time; voluntary surrender is permitted exemption from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Arrest them when found; allow surrender for mercy.

sentences.zh: 請廣、潮、肇、嘉諸府州山場荒地，令無業遊民報墾，永不昇科，庶衣食有資，免流匪僻。

translations.literal: He asked that in Guang, Chaozhou, Zhaoqing, and Jiaying prefectures mountain wasteland be opened for land reclamation by idle wanderers, never to be taxed in perpetuity, so that they might have food and clothing and wandering bandits be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed tax-free reclamation in mountain wastes for vagrants to curb banditry.

sentences.zh: 」如議行。

translations.literal: " This was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved.

sentences.zh: 入覲，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He came to audience and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，湖南瑤趙金龍倡亂，廣東連州瑤聞風蠢動，遣兵防剿。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year the Yao Zhao Jinlong of Hunan raised rebellion; the Yao of Lianzhou in Guangdong stirred at the news, and troops were sent to guard and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 12 Hunan Yao rebel Zhao Jinlong rose; Guangdong Lianzhou Yao stirred, and troops were sent.

sentences.zh: 五月，鴻賓赴連州，三路進兵，雖有斬獲，兵弁傷亡多，疏請俟湖南事竣進剿，詔斥任賊蔓延；

translations.literal: In the fifth month Hongbin went to Lianzhou and advanced on three routes; though there were kills and captures, many officers and soldiers were killed and wounded; he memorialized asking to wait until Hunan affairs were finished before advancing in suppression; an edict rebuked him for letting the bandits spread;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he attacked from three routes with heavy casualties and asked to wait for Hunan; the court rebuked him for letting rebels spread;

sentences.zh: 提督劉榮慶衰庸，不早糾劾，嚴議革職，改留任。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Liu Rongqing was decrepit and incompetent and had not been impeached early; after severe deliberation he was stripped of office, changed to retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rongqing incompetence drew severe censure but retention in office.

sentences.zh: 命尚書禧恩等由湖南移師赴粵剿辦，禧恩言：「粵兵多食鴉片，不耐山險，鴻賓陳奏不實。

translations.literal: Minister Xi En and others were ordered to move troops from Hunan to Guangdong to suppress; Xi En said: "Guangdong troops mostly eat opium and cannot endure mountain hardship; Hongbin reports are not true.
translations.idiomatic: Xi En moved troops from Hunan and said Guangdong soldiers were opium-addicted and Hongbin lied;

sentences.zh: 」褫職逮治，遣戍烏魯木齊。

translations.literal: " He was stripped of office, arrested and tried, and banished to Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongbin was stripped, tried, and exiled to Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 十四年，釋還，予編修。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was released and restored as Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was released and made Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 家居久之，二十年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home a long time and died in the twentieth year.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement long and died in year 20.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宣宗初政，勵精求治。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the beginning of Daoguang reign he strove to govern diligently.
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes: Early Daoguang sought diligent rule.

sentences.zh: 孫玉庭、蔣攸銛並以老成膺分陝之寄，大事多以諮決。

translations.literal: Sun Yuting and Jiang Youxian both, as seasoned men, received the trust of frontier appointment, and major affairs were mostly decided by consulting them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuting and Jiang Youxian, as veterans, were trusted on major decisions.

sentences.zh: 其時鹽、河、漕皆積困，玉庭持重，晚稍模棱。

translations.literal: At that time salt, rivers, and grain transport were all deeply exhausted; Yuting was weighty in manner, and in his later years somewhat equivocal.
translations.idiomatic: Salt, rivers, and transport were exhausted; Yuting was steady but grew equivocal late in life.

sentences.zh: 攸銛直行己意，眷注遂衰，然其汲引人才，識量遠矣。

translations.literal: Youxian acted straight by his own will, and imperial favor therefore waned, yet in drawing up talent his vision was far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Youxian's blunt ways cost favor, yet his eye for talent was far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 李鴻賓初以建言驟起，後乃簠簋不飭，貽海疆隱患。

translations.literal: Li Hongbin at first rose swiftly through remonstrance, but later was corrupt in his charge and bequeathed hidden troubles on the maritime frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongbin rose on memorials but later corrupted office and seeded coastal troubles.

sentences.zh: 三人皆不能以功名終，公私之殊，不可概論也。

translations.literal: None of the three could end in official success; the difference between public and private virtue cannot be discussed in one breath.
translations.idiomatic: None finished honorably; public and private virtue must not be lumped together.
